# How long does KDP review take after you press Publish? The timeline we plan every launch around

We publish short eBooks through Amazon Kindle Direct Publishing (KDP) — most recently [The Art of AI Monks](https://aniccaai.com/the-art-of-ai-monks), a 71-page PDF and EPUB with 10 chapters and 4 worksheets — and the most common planning mistake we see, including in our own early launches, is treating "Publish" as the launch. It is not. Publish starts a review, and then a set of separate clocks: the detail page, search visibility, the free sample, and price changes do not all arrive together. On 20 November 2026 we re-read KDP's official [Timelines](https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G202173620) and [Book Status](https://kdp.amazon.com/en_US/help/topic/G200627450) pages in full. Every duration below is KDP's own published estimate as those pages read on that date. KDP states plainly that the timelines are estimates only, and we treat them that way in our planning: as the outside window to allow, not as a promise about any one title.

## What is KDP's headline answer?

After you submit a book or an update for publication, KDP says it takes 3 business days for the book or update to be live on Amazon. Books are processed in the order they were received, and the time depends on the book type and the marketplace — Amazon.com and Amazon.de do not necessarily move together. One exception dominates everything else: for low-content books, such as journals or notebooks, reviews may take 3 to 4 weeks to complete, which KDP attributes to higher-than-normal publishing volumes. If your title is low-content, the 3-business-day figure is simply the wrong number to plan around.

KDP also closes the most tempting shortcut. Your book is processed in order, and reaching out to Customer Support will not expedite the review process. While a book is In Review, reviews cannot be expedited or canceled. In our workflow that means the schedule is fixed at the moment we press Publish, so all of our checking — files, metadata, categories, and the AI-content disclosure we work through in our [KDP AI disclosure checklist](https://aniccaai.com/blog/ebook-publishing-kdp-ai-disclosure-checklist) — happens before submission, not after.

## How long does a new eBook take, step by step?

For a new Kindle eBook, KDP's Timelines page breaks the wait into pieces. The detail page appears in up to 72 hours, and the cover thumbnail runs on the same up-to-72-hours clock. If this is the first title you are publishing on KDP, each of those can take up to 5 days instead. Being Live and being findable are still two different events: your book is displayed in search results up to 72 hours after it is live. The "Read Sample" — the Look Inside feature — is the slowest piece of all, at 7 to 8 business days. If you also publish a print edition, the eBook is linked to the paperback or hardcover edition 48 hours to 1 week after each edition is live, and KDP notes it usually takes 3 to 5 days for customer reviews to be copied from the print edition to the eBook edition.

Our practical reading of that table is that a launch has at least three separate "done" moments. First the book is Live and purchasable. Then, up to 72 hours later, a reader searching Amazon can actually find it. Then, more than a week later, the sample a hesitant reader relies on is in place. Announcing a book on the first moment and judging it on the third moment's evidence mixes up three different clocks, so we check each one separately, on its own date.

## How long does a new paperback or hardcover take?

Print runs slower at the edges, even when the headline is similar. A new paperback or hardcover detail page appears in up to 72 hours for Amazon.com and up to 5 days for other marketplaces — and KDP flags one long outlier: it can take up to 30 days for the detail page to appear on Amazon.ca. The "in stock" display follows the same pattern, up to 72 hours for Amazon.com and up to 5 days elsewhere. For accounts without a previously published book, publishing may take up to 6 days. The low-content warning applies here in full as well: those reviews are taking longer than usual and may take 3 to 4 weeks.

Two print clocks surprise people who plan only for the listing itself. The back cover image takes 7 to 10 business days to appear on the detail page, so a page can be live and purchasable while still showing no back cover. The print "Read Sample" takes 9 to 10 business days, longer than the eBook's 7 to 8. Linking a print edition to the eBook edition takes 48 hours to 1 week after each version is live, and KDP notes the editions link automatically only if the metadata for both editions exactly matches — one more reason we copy titles, subtitles and author names character for character between editions instead of retyping them.

## How long do updates to a live book take?

Corrections are not instant either, and each kind of change has its own timeline. For eBooks, updates to author name and contributors, title, description, publisher, ISBN and keywords appear in 72 hours. Category updates also take 72 hours, with the caveat that sales rank can take up to 1 week to update after a category change. Manuscript and cover updates take 72 hours, the updated "Read Sample" takes 7 to 8 business days, and a list price update is the fastest change on the page at 24 hours. Unpublishing is not immediate: an unpublished eBook becomes unavailable for purchase in 24 to 72 hours and unsearchable in a minimum of one week. A republished eBook becomes available again in 12 hours for titles in English and 48 hours for titles in other languages.

For paperback and hardcover, manuscript and cover updates take up to 72 hours — again with the low-content exception of up to 3 to 4 weeks — and the updated "Read Sample" takes 9 to 10 business days. Print list price updates take 72 hours to 5 business days depending on the significance of the change, and until the new price appears, royalties on retail orders are still calculated on the previous list price and its royalty rate. That last point connects directly to the math in our [KDP royalty unit economics guide](https://aniccaai.com/blog/ebook-publishing-kdp-royalty-unit-economics-2026): a price change is a plan for next week, not a lever for today. Because every update re-enters review timing, we batch corrections into one careful submission instead of dribbling out small fixes day by day.

## What do the Bookshelf statuses actually mean?

KDP's Book Status page defines the labels you watch while all of this runs. **Draft** means you have started entering book details but have not submitted; you can edit freely. **In Review** means KDP is checking the book against its formatting and content guidelines; you cannot make changes, and the review cannot be expedited or canceled. The signal most often misread is a book that was In Review and is back in Draft: KDP says that means it found things that need to be updated, and the details are in the email it sent. The fix is to update the book to meet the guidelines and resubmit, which starts review again. **Publishing** means the book has passed review and is being published; changes are still locked. **Live** means the book is published and available for purchase, and certain details can then be edited.

Three Live variants cover the update cycle. **Live — with unpublished changes** means you edited a Live book but have not submitted the edits yet, so readers still see the old version until you submit and the updates pass review. **Live — Updates in review** means the book stays on sale while your recent changes are reviewed; you cannot make additional changes meanwhile. **Live — Updates publishing** means those changes are being published and will appear shortly. **Blocked** is different in kind: the book does not meet the content guidelines and is blocked from publishing or editing, and a blocked title cannot be deleted from the Bookshelf. KDP sends an email with the specific reason, and replying directly to that email is the stated route to its support team. We keep that distinction in our notes because Draft-after-review and Blocked look similar on a tired evening but call for opposite actions: edit and resubmit in the first case, work through the email in the second.

## How do pre-orders change the timeline?

Pre-orders add a hard deadline on top of the review clocks. Pre-order titles are typically reviewed and published within 24 to 72 hours, or up to 5 days if it is your first title on KDP. The final manuscript must be uploaded and submitted at least 72 hours before the release date — 5 days before, for a first title — and you cannot update the manuscript or book details inside that final window. KDP points publishers to the timer at the top of the title setup page in the Bookshelf as the most accurate countdown for a given title. For print books with a scheduled release date, the same discipline applies in a longer form: the final manuscript is due at least five days before the scheduled release date, and review of the book takes up to 72 hours. In both cases the lesson is the same: the release date is chosen backwards from the submission deadline, not forwards from the day the draft feels finished.

## How do we plan a launch around these clocks?

Our checklist is short because the timelines leave little to improvise. We submit with the full window still available — at minimum the 3 business days to Live, plus up to 72 hours for search, plus 7 to 10 business days before we treat the sample as part of the offer. We verify in order: Bookshelf status first, then the detail page itself on the marketplace we care about, then search, then the sample, each recorded with its date rather than assumed from the previous step. We batch every known correction into a single update, because each submission restarts its own 72-hour clock. And we never set a public launch date, an ad start, or a price-dependent promotion inside the window where KDP says the relevant piece may not exist yet. None of this makes review faster. It makes the wait legible, which is what a small publisher actually needs.

More of our field notes are in the [eBook Publishing hub](https://aniccaai.com/blog/c/ebook-publishing), including how we classify AI-generated and AI-assisted content before publishing and how we read royalty statements without mistaking royalty for profit.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can you speed up a KDP review by contacting support?

No. KDP states that books are processed in the order received and that reaching out to Customer Support will not expedite the review process. While a book is In Review, the review cannot be expedited or canceled, and you cannot make changes until it leaves that status.

### Why is my book Live but not showing in Amazon search?

Because search runs on a separate clock. KDP allows up to 72 hours after a book is live for it to be displayed in search results. Check the detail page directly first; a missing search result inside that window is a timeline, not a failure.

### Why did my book go from In Review back to Draft?

KDP says that means it found things that need to be updated. The specifics are in the email KDP sent. Update the book to meet the formatting and content guidelines, then resubmit it for publication, and it will be reviewed again.

### How long does a price change take on KDP?

For an eBook, a list price update appears in 24 hours. For paperback and hardcover, it takes 72 hours to 5 business days depending on the significance of the change, and royalties on orders placed before the update are still based on the previous price and rate.

### How long does the free sample take to appear?

The eBook "Read Sample" takes 7 to 8 business days for a new publication. The paperback and hardcover "Read Sample" takes 9 to 10 business days. The back cover image on a print detail page also takes 7 to 10 business days.
